title: pellegrinia lanceolata
intro: Pellegrinia lanceolata, commonly known as the Lance-leaved Pellegrinia, is a plant species within the family Rutaceae, native to Madagascar. This plant has been traditionally used for its health benefits, including its antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and antiseptic properties, making it a valuable resource in folk medicine. The therapeutic actions of Pellegrinia lanceolata are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including alkaloids, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its potential in treating various health conditions. However, further research is needed to confirm the full extent of its health benefits and therapeutic actions.
